declarations.description:
Metro Button Component

A standard push button implementing the Metro design language with distinctive
visual feedback and interactions. Features include:
- Color inversion on hover (foreground becomes background)
- Accent color variant for primary actions
- Tilt animation effect on pointer interaction
- Keyboard navigation support (Enter/Space activation)
- Full ARIA accessibility support

Use this component for standard button actions in forms, toolbars, or any
interactive UI element that triggers an action when clicked.

The button is form-associated: inside a `<form>` it follows native button
semantics. The `type` property controls behavior (`submit` by default,
`reset` clears the owner form, `button` performs no form action). The form
owner is submitted via `requestSubmit()` so constraint validation runs;
note that `formaction`/`formmethod` submitter overrides are not supported.

Metro Dropdown Button Component

A button that reveals a dropdown menu when clicked. Supports labeled buttons
with optional icons and configurable menu placement. Items in the dropdown
should use the CSS class "menu-item" on their root element.

Features:
- Labeled button with optional icon
- Configurable dropdown placement (top/bottom)
- Animated chevron rotation when opened
- Menu enter/exit animations
- Click outside to close
- Keyboard navigation support
- ARIA attributes for accessibility (menu, expanded state)

Use for action menus, filter options, or any UI requiring a collapsible list
of selectable items attached to a button trigger.

declarations.description:
Metro Repeat Button Component

A specialized button that repeatedly fires click events while being held down.
Ideal for increment/decrement controls, volume adjustment, or any action that
should repeat when the user holds the button.

Features:
- Configurable initial delay before repeat starts (default: 500ms)
- Configurable repeat interval between clicks (default: 100ms)
- Color inversion on hover
- Accent color variant for primary actions
- Tilt animation effect on pointer interaction
- Keyboard activation support
- Automatically stops repeating when released or on pointer leave

Use for media controls (volume, seek), numeric inputs (spinner buttons),
or any action that benefits from rapid repetition.

declarations.description:
Metro Content Dialog Component

A customizable modal dialog for displaying content with optional title,
content area, and button slot. Uses the View Transitions API for smooth
coordinated enter/exit animations of the dialog and backdrop. Suitable
for forms, confirmations, or any custom content.

Features:
- Optional title header with border separator
- Scrollable content area for long content
- Dedicated button slot for action buttons
- Optional close button (can be disabled for required dialogs)
- View Transition-powered enter/exit animations
- Backdrop click to close (when closable)
- Escape to close, focus moves into the dialog on open and back to the opener
  on close, and Tab stays inside the dialog while it is open
- ARIA dialog role with modal support
- Programmatic show/hide API

Use for custom modal content that requires user interaction or attention.
For simple message dialogs, consider MetroMessageDialog instead.

members.description:
Returns focus to the element that opened the dialog. A custom-element host is

members.name: #applyChange
members.description:
Applies a property change via View Transitions with headless fallback.
Uses the applied-flag pattern to ensure DOM updates even when
startViewTransition skips the callback (headless browsers).
Awaits both updateCallbackDone and finished to properly clean up
the transition before returning.
Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the transition is skipped rather than
sped up, so the change lands with no entrance motion at all.

Opens the dialog with enter animation and dispatches show event.
Uses View Transitions for a coordinated backdrop + dialog animation.
Escape is listened for on the document from the first moment, so a key
pressed while the entrance is still running dismisses the dialog. Focus
moves in only after `open` is applied: the dialog is hidden until then, so an
earlier focus call would land on the opener.

Uses View Transitions for a coordinated backdrop + dialog animation.

Metro Flyout Component

A floating popup panel that appears relative to a target element.
Features a 3D perspective animation via View Transitions and backdrop overlay.
The Flyout is positioned programmatically and is ideal for contextual menus,
tooltips, or any popup content.

- 3D perspective enter animation via View Transitions
- Four placement options: top, bottom, left, right
- Backdrop overlay for modal-like behavior
- Escape to close, focus moves into the flyout on open and back to the opener on close
- Automatic positioning based on target element
- Fixed positioning to appear above other content

Unlike MetroTooltip, the Flyout requires a target element and is
designed for more substantial content like menus or forms.

declarations.description:
Windows Phone semantic zoom: a detailed view and an overview of the same content, switched by pinch, Ctrl+Scroll, or the hint button. ## Group contract Content goes in the `zoomed-in` and `zoomed-out` slots. Whatever element starts a group carries `data-group-key`, in both views, with the same key in each one, so the overview is a map of the list rather than a second dataset: ```html

A

…rows of group A…
``` With that in place: - `scrollToGroup(key)` zooms in when the overview is up, then aligns that group with the start edge of the element that actually scrolls it — the inline start of a horizontal scroller, the top edge of a vertical one. - Tapping a `[data-group-key]` element of the overview re-enters the list at that group. - `currentGroup` reports the group at the start line of the axis the list scrolls on (top for a vertical list, inline start for a horizontal one), and `groupchanged` fires when it changes: bubbles and composed, `detail: { key: string | null }`. The read measures the top edge, so it describes a vertically scrolled list. Keys are matched against the content assigned to the slot, following the slots it passes through, so a group header inside a slotted component counts as well as a direct child. A group is measured where it draws, so the keyed element has to sit in the normal flow of the list: a header pinned by `position: sticky` always reads as already aligned, and scrolling back to it then does nothing.
